What makes it Albastini

Heavy condensed caps could belong to any sports or gaming brand. It becomes Albastini through what it sets: outlined rank numerals, tabular prize columns, a single-font width-axis discipline, and the real copy.

Weakest point (honest)

On its own this is the most generic board. Don't judge the type apart from the covers, ladder and fixture.

Anatomy
  • Edge — 12px radius (the card corner), not a pill
  • Keyline — 1.5px inset, like a printed card border
  • Chip — the 11-point disc carries the arrow (the one non-generic part)
  • Hover — fill sweeps in 240ms, label +3px, chip +4px and tilts −12° like a dealt card
  • Press — 1px down, inner shadow; Focus — 3px ring in the scene's contrast colour
Related controls (same geometry)
Live — hover, press, Tab to focus

Contrast: black on yellow 16:1 · white ring on blue 8:1 · blue ring on paper 8:1 · yellow ring on night 12.5:1.

Could this belong to another brand?
Passes, narrowly — depends on the chip.
What makes it Albastini

12px card corner, printed keyline, and an arrow carried by the 11-point disc that tilts like a dealt card on hover.

Weakest point (honest)

A rounded rectangle with an arrow is common. Remove the chip and this is generic. If review finds the chip too small a signal, the next pass adds a card-corner cut to the keyline.

How uneven photography becomes intentional
  1. Cut-out on plate (David, MJeshi) — figure bottom-anchored, shoulders bleed past the keyline, rank numeral sits behind them.
  2. Scene in a window (Bedadi) — his real photo, edge-graded into arena blue by a vignette; numeral sits in front, outlined, so the face stays clear.
  3. Shared — keyline, wave-cut nameplate, rank numeral, placement chip, collector index, prize in tabular numerals. Any future photo picks one of the two modes.
  4. Rank by scale (500 / 430 / 380 px numeral) and keyline contrast; the crown marks first place only. No medal colours.

What these photos can't do: David is 720×880 (backlit selfie, soft at 2×); Bedadi's crop is 480×600; MJeshi was separated from a poster. The frame unifies them; it can't repair them. Better originals drop in with no redesign.

Tried and rejected: auto-cutting Bedadi — the model kept his white throne chair and gold drape (a throne is off-brand), so he stays a real scene.

Could this belong to another brand?
Passes strongly.
What makes it Albastini

Rank numeral as architecture, wave-cut nameplate, keyline, crown on first place only, collector index. These could only be Albastini champions.

Weakest point (honest)

Source photography is uneven and the frame cannot repair it: Bedadi (scene) and the cut-outs remain visibly different even after grading. Better originals would close the gap.

  • A ladder, not a pricing table. Three columns of cards would read as a plan comparison. One axis of length reads as ranking.
  • Data-driven. Rendered from tournamentPrizeStructure — change the amounts there and lengths, labels and numbers follow. Nothing is typed twice.
  • The wave is the bar's end — the same curve that crosses every card face.
  • Tabular numerals right-align the prizes into a true column (see Board 01).
  • Motion: one SLIDE per bar (scaleX, 620ms, 90ms stagger), once on entry; numbers never count up. Reduced motion: bars appear at full length.
  • Accessibility: real ordered list with the amounts as text; the bars are decorative.
Could this belong to another brand?
Passes.
What makes it Albastini

Proportional bars ending in the card wave, outlined ranks, tabular amounts, driven by the real prize structure.

Weakest point (honest)

Horizontal bars resemble a bar chart by nature; the wave end and rank numerals are the differentiators.

↑ = scaled up: orange +8.5% (smallest source, 848 px) and red +2%. Everything else scales down by 0.4–3.9%.

After — normalised (click)

Same canvas, same centre, same pivot. Front and back share one 1024×1536 frame; the dashed box is the canonical card.

Residual: silhouettes now differ by at most 3.6% in width and 2.5% in height (the back is the narrow one) — down from 12.5% width / 6.2% ratio spread as supplied. At the flip's midpoint the card is edge-on, so this is invisible.

Before — as supplied (click)

The jump you'd have shipped. Cropped to their own edges at equal width, the back is 6% taller than the front: the dashed line (front's edge) is overrun on every turn.

Fixed without cropping, stretching or inventing pixels: originals untouched in assets-source/; normalised masters are generated by scripts/normalize-cards.mjs.

Could this belong to another brand?
Passes — infrastructure.
What makes it Albastini

Makes the approved back and fronts behave as one physical card.

Weakest point (honest)

Residual 3.5% width difference remains by design (padding, not cropping). Orange ace is upscaled 8.5%.

Ready to

INGIA UWANJANI TUCHEZE.
  • The crown token is the anchor — the official token cropped from the official mark (circular mask, no redraw), at poster scale, ringed by the same dashed perforation as the 11-point chip.
  • The type crosses it. "READY TO PLAY?" overlaps the token so word and object are one composition, not a headline beside a picture.
  • A full hand bleeds off the bottom — five official cards, fanned, cut by the frame like a hand held low at the table.
  • The phrase is the signature: INGIA UWANJANI TUCHEZE. with a chip bullet; exactly one full stop, at the end.
  • Footer = last line of the poster, not a new section: mark, phrase, links, language. Only verified destinations; no social or legal links until supplied.
  • Held frame. It stops. Nothing loops at the end of the page.
Could this belong to another brand?
Passes with caution.
What makes it Albastini

The crown token as anchor with the dashed perforation ring, type crossing it, a full hand bleeding off the frame.

Weakest point (honest)

Huge type on dark with a fan is a poster formula; the official crown and chip ring are what hold it to Albastini.

  • Named from the table, not from animation libraries: deal · turn · slide · settle. Each scene owns one hero verb; the rest is settle or still.
  • Never: looping float, springy overshoot, letter-by-letter split text, scroll-jacking, parallax on everything. All motion = transform/opacity.
Could this belong to another brand?
Passes by use, not by motion.
What makes it Albastini

Verbs named from the table (deal, turn, slide, settle), each assigned to one place, with reduced-motion equivalents.

Weakest point (honest)

Slide and settle are ordinary motions; their meaning comes from where they're used.

Glassmorphism / blurred navGeneric; hurts contrast over photography. The nav is a keylined object instead.
Noisy / grain gradientsOnly one gradient exists: brand blue → blue mixed with black (the arena).
Random 3D & tilt-everything3D is reserved for one place: a card turning. Nothing else has depth cues.
Brutalist / marquee typeAlbastini is energetic, not anti-design. Type is composed, not shouted in loops.
Custom cursor everywhereToken only over cards that act (select / flip). Native cursor elsewhere.
Cursor on hero cardsThey do nothing on click; a 'VIEW' label would be a lie (D6).
Medal colours (gold/silver/bronze)Rank = scale, numeral and keyline; one yellow, one paper, one dimmer paper (D7).
Thrones, trophies, confetti, money graphicsCasino/pageant cues. Prestige comes from scale and real faces.
Literal card → phone morphDistorts both objects; looks like a tech demo (D4). Deck hand-off instead.
Pill buttons24 pills was the single most template-like trait. Replaced by the card edge.
Letter-by-letter split textDelays reading; reads as a reel. Headlines settle as whole phrases.
Magnetic buttons, cursor-follow blobsFast chase motion; no physical meaning at a card table.
Preloader / intro screenContent is the first paint; nothing makes anyone wait.
WebGLNothing in the concept needs it; CSS 3D covers the one flip.
Bento grids / feature cardsReintroduces the generic section stack the CEO removed.
Stock or generated peopleReal photographs only (3 winners). Community slot stays empty.
Auto-matted Bedadi cut-outTried. The model kept his white throne chair and gold drape; a throne is off-brand. He is shown as the real scene instead.
Proportional numerals for prizesColumns drift; tabular numerals align (Board 01).

If you approve

M1 builds the foundations: tokens (edge, keyline, chip, four motion verbs), scene themes, focus system and the budget scripts — then nav and buttons (M2).

Needs your eye first
  • Is the chip a strong enough signal for buttons and nav, or should the keyline get a card-corner cut?
  • Bedadi as a scene window beside two cut-outs: unified enough, or do you want better originals before M7?
  • Finale: crown at poster scale — right, or too heavy?
